contexts.text: Kiss me my son () = whether he could be united. To kiss = unition and conjunction from affection. Kissing, which is an external thing, is nothing else than the affection of conjunction, which is an internal one: they also correspond.
He approached and kissed him () = presence and unition... To kiss = unition or conjunction from affection. Illustrated.
To kiss the Son () = to be conjoined with the Lord by the faith of love.
Let justice and peace kiss () = let them conjoin themselves.
They are said to kiss the calves (), that is, embrace magic, and adjoin themselves to it.
Every mouth which hath not kissed Baal (). To kiss = to conjoin themselves from affection, thus to worship.
Jacob kissed Rachel () = love towards interior truths. To kiss = unition and conjunction from affection; consequently love...
And kissed him () = initiation. To kiss = conjunction from affection; here, initiation to this conjunction; for initiation is what precedes conjunction.
And hast not permitted me to kiss my sons and my daughters () = disjunction... as to truths and goods.

(Laban) kissed his sons and his daughters () = the acknowledgement of these Truths, and of the affections of the same. To kiss = conjunction from affection, consequently acknowledgement; for where there is conjunction by good and truth, there is the acknowledgement of them.
Conjunction from affection produces kissing (by the correspondence)...
He kissed him () = interior conjunction from love. To kiss = conjunction from love; here, interior conjunction.
Upon thy mouth all my people shall kiss () = that everything there shall be under obedience to him. To kiss upon his mouth = to acknowledge and do what he commands, thus to obey.
He kissed all his brethren () = adjunction from grace. To kiss = conjunction from affection; here, adjunction from grace. Explained.

He kissed them () = conjunction from the affection of truth... because there follows he embraced them, by which is signified conjunction from the affection of good; for embracing is a more interior and thence closer affection than kissing, as is the affection of good than the affection of truth.
He kissed him () = the first conjunction. To kiss = conjunction from affection; here, the first conjunction, because in what follows it treats of a closer conjunction.
And kissed him () = the affection of conjunction. To kiss = conjunction from affection. AC 8664.
The wings kissed one another () = to act conjointly and unanimously.
The two Angels embraced and kissed each other. TCR 386.
He then kissed her, and said. Now thou art mine...
From the mouths of their wives which they kiss.
They kiss nature as the creatress of the universe. TCR 508:3.
Robbers, who kiss each other when they are at robberies...
The satan kissed her, and said. Oh my Adonis!
Then the goods kiss each other and conjoin themselves.
He kisses sin daily, like...
The black cow kissed her...
She kissed him, and then he was tortured...
See Charles XII.
The wings kissed one another = the consociation and conjunction of all things there by the Lord.
To kiss the calves = to become merely natural.
Kiss ye the Son = conjunction with the Lord by love. To kiss = conjunction from love. AE 850:3.
See Embrace.
On Miracles. The Angels kissed me on account of the things which I had said...
